There are many personality flaws, but this is one to avoid when you catch the signs, both in your personal life and when nominating candidates for federal office.

Don't disagree but it's not reading between the lines it's explicit! Nothing about Platner is subtle. He's a manipulative narciccist. He's trying to save face by making himself a martyr. Martyrdom is often persuasive so this is a bad development for Ds. Also totally predictable.
Yeah this is pretty bearish for Democrats. Did the conspiracy extend to Chuck Schumer making him get a Totenkopf tattoo?

I have more thoughts about Maine. I do think a relatively progressive replacement would make sense, both in terms of being more respectful of the primary result and in not alienating Platner's voters. But some sort of process that involves voter participation would be best.

His greater leverage is really in the fact that he does have a lot of loyal voters and you don’t necessarily want him to be an aggrieved party, which gets back to the earlier point about it inherently being hard to bargain with assholes.

His leverage is also kinda fake because if he's down 10 points in the polls or whatever and going to lose anyway, optimal strategy is to write the race off and not undermine the national brand by defending him in any way.

Optimal strategy is that Maine Democrats pre-commit to nominating a different candidate as opposed to an alleged rapist and will run him/her on a write-in line regardless of what Platner does. It's unlikely to come to that IMO but that greatly reduces his leverage.

He does sort of have some leverage, but it's more toward the Mutually Assured Destruction side and also he should be pretty happy to settle for outcomes in which he's able to start a Substack or whatever as opposed to being a total pariah.
I don't know if you should call this the Platner Paradox or whatever but one the problems with bargaining with crazy people is that they're, well, crazy.
